{{Short description|French mining engineer}}
[[File:Theodore moutard.jpg|thumb|Photo by André Bujeaud]]
'''Théodore Florentin Moutard''' (27 July 1827 – 13 March 1901) was a French mining engineer who worked at the [[Mines Paris - PSL|École des Mines]] and contributed to mathematical geometry. The Moutard transformation in inverse geometry is named after him.

Moutard was born in [[Soultz-Haut-Rhin|Soultz]], Haut-Rhin, to Florentin and Elisabeth BERNOU. He was educated at the [[École polytechnique|École Polytechnique]] and graduated in 1846 and entered the École des Mines and after graduating in 1849 he joined the Mining corps but was discharged in 1852 as he refused to take the oath required following the overthrow of [[Napoleon III]]. He joined back in 1870 and became a professor of mechanics at the École des Mines in 1875. He was also an examiner for the École Polytechnique from 1883. Moutard contributed to the ''La grande encyclopédie'' and his mathematical work was on algebraic surfaces and differential geometry. He collaborated with [[Jean-Victor Poncelet|Victor Poncelet]] on elliptic functions.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Algèbre des fonctions elliptiques et géométrie des ovales cartésiennes|author1=Barbin, Évelyne  | author2= Guitart, René| journal=Revue d'histoire des mathématiques|volume= 7 |year=2001| issue= 2| pages= 161–205|language=fr|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/RHM_2001__7_2_161_0.pdf}}.</ref>

He was made Commander of the [[Legion of Honour|Legion of Honor]] in 1899. Moutard married twice and had two sons and two daughters. One of his sons was Douard Julien Moutard (1877–1948). One daughter Berthe married the mathematician [[Paul Matthieu Hermann Laurent|Hermann Laurent]]. A daughter from his second marriage, Elisabeth married André Bujeaud, a politician and photographer, in 1868.
<ref>{{cite web |last1=Le Ferrand |first1=Hervé |title=Au sujet du mathématicien Hermann Laurent (1841-1908) |website=Hal |date=November 2014 |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01084722v2| access-date=April 27, 2024}}.</ref>
